To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Sar1 is an important regulator of ER morphology and that Sar1 regulates the selection of cargo for export from the ER.
Sar1, in the absence other cytosolic factors, generates ER-derived tubular structures, that resemble transitional ER elements, that initiate COPII cargo selection.
Sar1, a key regulator of the COPII protein transport machinery, is required to generate ER export sites that are competent for cargo selection and export from cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the transport of proteins from the endoplamic reticulum (ER) to the golgi apparatus in mammalian cells.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the transport of proteins from the endoplamic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus in mammalian cells.
the mechanisms of membrane protein sorting and transport from the endoplamic reticulum to the Golgi complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Sar1, a small GTPase that is activated by guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs) and inactivated by GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs), regulates the formation of ER export sites that are required for the selection of cargo for COPII-mediated vesicle formation.
Sar1 is required for cargo selection and the assembly of transitional ER export sites, which are dynamic tubular structures that are essential for ER export.

Sar1, in addition to its role as a GTPase in cargo selection, also functions as a key regulator in the generation of transitional ER tubular domains that are the sites of COPII coat-mediated cargo selection and export from ER to Golgi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Sar1 GTPase is a critical factor for the selection of cargo for transport from the ER and for the formation of the ER export site.
Sar1 GTPase is the master regulator of COPII coat assembly and ER export.
the Sar1 GTPase coordinates cargo selection with ER export site assembly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Sar1, in addition to its well-established function in ER export, is also required for cargo selection.
Sar1 is not just a simple GTPase that cycles between GTP and GDP states.
Sar1 GTPase is a key player in the formation and maintenance of ER export sites, and that the Sar1 GTP cycle coordinates cargo selection with ER export site assembly.
